name: Vision
desc: Visions are external magical foci bestowed by Celestia and The Seven upon Allogenes, a small minority of people with strong desires, allowing them to channel a specific elemental power. Every wielder of a Vision is able to attain godhood and ascend to Celestia.

customize.text:
Many millennia ago, the world was ruled by the Seven Sovereigns — seven elemental dragons, one for each element. One day, the first throne of eternity, the
known as the Heavenly Principles, appeared in the heavens. The Heavenly Principles declared war on the elemental dragons, and after forty years of battle, the seven sovereigns were defeated, and the seven nations submitted to the heavens. The Heavenly Principles stole the power of the defeated Sovereigns, used it to create divine thrones, and established the cycle of seven. Six thousand years ago, the primordial ruler of Teyvat, Dragon King Nibelung, returned to Teyvat, igniting the War of Funerary Flames. During this conflict, Phanes was wounded and lost some of their functions, so they could no longer use their absolute authority to suppress the original order of this world. Using the remains of a third Descender, who had sacrificed himself for the sake of resurrecting Anastasya Feodorovna, the future Tsaritsa of Snezhnaya, the Heavenly Principles created the Gnoses, one for each of the seven divine thrones. The stolen dragons' authority became the source of the Archons' powers, and humanity began to harness a portion of this power. Whenever a person's wishes reached the heavens, the seven overseers of the material realm were duty-bound to grant them a
Though they might know nothing of who or what wish had stepped into the threshold of the sacred, the Seven Archons still had to impart a shattered shard of their mastery to that person.

Visions are external magical foci that grant the ability to wield one of the seven elements altered by the Heavenly Principles: Pyro, Hydro, Cryo, Anemo, Geo, Electro, and Dendro. The seven elements that a Vision bearer can command are linked to the Seven Sovereigns. People marked by the attention of Celestia are named allogenes, which is a secret that only Archons are privy to. For millennia, it was believed that a Vision was a divine favor, and that allogenes would ascend to Celestia to become gods themselves. In reality, allogenes serve as "fuel" for creating humans modeled after humanity as recorded in Celestia's database. An allogene's
and
are disembodied from their physical body, transforming them into "Vectors of Fate" that guide civilization to a better future. To Celestia, this is the definition of transcending and attaining immortality and constitutes the sole calling and value of an allogene. The world in which the "Divine Throne," Celestia's integrated computational array, was born was destroyed, and it couldn't receive information from beyond. The progress was possible only by feeding the evolution of civilization back into the system. When the Archons and the rulers of the seven kingdoms underwent the "Trials of Usurpation" to halt the expansion of the Holy Soil unleashed by the Ruler of Death, the "Divine Throne" granted them a final forty-two days. During this time, they were permitted to select one allogene each to ascend to Celestia as the final record of this civilization.

A Vision is a round, diamond-shaped, or oval artifact that bears the symbol of its corresponding element. Since all Fontainians possess Arkhe, a unique power that drives the region's various mechanisms, this is reflected in the appearance of their Visions. An exception is Furina, whose Vision incorporates the designs of both Pneuma and Ousia. After the death of the owner, the Vision fades and becomes white and cloudy. After the user's death, Visions become masterless husks without any elemental power, and there's no known method of reawakening them, save for a tiny chance that it may resonate with another — and only one such "other" at a time. For instance, Kazuha, a wandering samurai from Inazuma, was able to briefly reignite the extinguished Vision of his fallen friend when their desires aligned. Similarly, Ningguang, the Tianquan of the Liyue Qixing, "reawakened" a dormant Vision she had discovered, just as she was ready to sell it. The exact process by which one obtains a Vision remains unknown, and for many, it simply appears out of thin air. Contrary to popular belief among people, the Archons do not give out Visions, but their receipt may be associated with the will of a person and the Archon's authority. For reasons unknown, no new Electro Visions were granted following the commencement of the Vision Hunt Decree in Inazuma. When the Dragon Sovereign Neuvillette fully restored his authority and set aside parts of himself, like the dragon-treasure hoards of old, he left them awaiting valiant humans to come and claim them. The first one to receive a Vision during Neuvillette's reign was Furina. A Vision can manifest a person's elemental power, much like how Oz appeared alongside Fischl after she received her Vision.

Allogenes held varying perspectives on these artifacts. Some view them as a mockery by the gods, while others see them as a form of divine recognition, a stark contrast to those who lack a Vision and often feel forsaken by the gods. Some use their Visions to assist others or aid in their work, whereas others attach no particular importance to them. A Vision reflects the ideals, aspirations, and dreams of its wielder even after the owner's death. This is why the involuntary loss of a Vision can lead to profound devastation, apathy, and amnesia, a fate that befell many during the Vision Hunt Decree in Inazuma. A warrior who once defended Konda Village seemed to lose a vital part of himself upon the loss of his Vision, becoming an entirely different person. A samurai who participated in the Vision Hunt Decree had been purchasing food rations for the local villagers out of his own pocket. However, when prices soared, his wages no longer sufficed, forcing him to take on debt. After his Vision was seized, the man forgot the events that had transpired, while the villagers accused him of misappropriating the rations for his own personal gain. A swordsman, who once dreamed of becoming the greatest in the world and trained his own disciples, forbade his students from practicing after his Vision was confiscated, leading them to believe that their master had been possessed by a demon. Previously, his sole purpose in life had been to become the finest swordsman, and he even crossed blades with his own mentor and friends. Once that ambition vanished, his soul was consumed by doubt, and in his struggle against his own inner fears, he descended into this state. The swordsman, fearing that his disciples might meet the same fate as he did, forbade them from training, but they remained steadfast in their commitment to follow him to the very end, even if it meant enduring suffering in the future.

Some Vision holders feel that their Visions steal pride originally due to them. Keqing, the Yuheng of the Liyue Qixing, has made numerous attempts to destroy her Vision. She left her Vision in a huge fire for three days and three nights, ran over it with a minecart full of rocks, and even hurled it from the heights of the Jade Chamber, but all her efforts proved futile. While a Vision cannot be lost or destroyed, its wielder may choose to voluntarily renounce both their goals and the Vision itself. Jiangxue, a descendant of the Yunlai Fishermen, one of the Eight Adepts, once used his power to commit evil deeds. Later, deeming himself unworthy, he cast his Vision aside. Diluc, a former captain of the Knights of Favonius, relinquished his Vision upon leaving Mondstadt following his father's death, only to reclaim it three years later. Furthermore, after losing a duel to Kujou Sara, Itto, along with his associate Kuki Shinobu, voluntarily surrendered his Vision during the Vision Hunt Decree. Visions share a profound bond with their wielders. For instance, the Traveler was able to perceive events involving Tartaglia after the latter left his Vision behind, as it had ceased to function reliably.

customize.text:
Long before the Heavenly Principles established the system of Visions, the three Moon Goddesses used ritual artifacts to communicate with their followers. These ceremonial objects, crafted in
harnessed a purer form of power distinct from the elemental energy tainted by the Heavenly Principles. Much like a Vision, a Moon Wheel is forged from the substance of a soul and is intrinsically linked to an individual's desires. However, unlike a Vision, this artifact from Nephilheim does not rely on the approval of the gods or the power of the Archons. One such bearer of a Lunar Wheel is the Lunar Envoy and angel, Zibai, who received the artifact from Istaroth, the Ruler of Time. Istaroth once placed before Zibai a crest engraved with the sigil of the moons which meant the angel no longer be just an agent of the Heavenly Principles but also an envoy of the moons as well. Initially, Zibai didn't accept this crest since she did not understand how such an extraneous crest could make the divine plan any more perfect, and believed her mission required no such supplement. In time, however, she came to realize that the love offered by the Heavenly Principles and that of the Moon Goddesses were not the same. While the Heavenly Principles would annihilate civilizations deemed insufficiently sacred, those that had strayed from their design, the moonlight offered solace to those that had suffered the withering light. When Zibai's own kingdom was destroyed, the moon-crest dropped onto her back like a falling tear. It was the same cold glow she had once beheld and turned down, yet it bestowed upon her the same tranquility and solace as the moonlight had long bestowed upon humanity.

Another possessor of a Moon Wheel is Ineffa — a divided part of the Eleventh Lord, "Mirror of the Dawning Morn." About two thousand years ago, following the dragons' defeat in the war against humanity, the consciousness of the Eleventh Lord, tormented by a choice, fractured into two parts: one, the Sovereign Ruler, sworn to take revenge on humanity, and the other, the malfunction, eager to find a new home. Lianca, the human foster daughter of another Sovereign Ruler, along with her companion from the Children of Echoes, integrated the Moon Wheel, which was left to Lianca by her mother, into this "malfunction," granting it a chance at a second life. Furthermore, Moon Wheels are held by inhabitants of Nod-Krai who are connected to the Moon Goddess, Columbina. Among them are Moonchanter Lauma, a descendant of the ancient Hyperboreans, who received her Moon Wheel at birth; Nefer, the successor to the Lunar Envoy Thoth; and the Fae, Flins and Linnea. Although the Fae, originally created from the remains of the Cryo Dragon, possess their own innate powers and have no need for external artifacts, Moon Wheels can serve to amplify these existing abilities.

Another artifact, similar to a Vision, is the Stellar Linchpin. Its origins are linked to the Third Descender, and wielding elemental energy, Stellar Linchpin-users often exhibit a unique kind of power that seems to come from beyond Teyvat. It's believed that, when a Stellar Linchpin manifests, impurities from the remains of the Third Descender get fixed in place. Such artifacts appear most frequently among the people of Snezhnaya, a nation intrinsically tied to the Third Descender. Upon its emergence, a Stellar Linchpin has the potential to save the life of its bearer. Thus, the appearance of the Stellar Linchpin rebooted the sentient mechanism, Sandrone, who had been killed during a battle against the second of the Fatui Harbingers, and also saved the Fae, Vesna, who had been poisoned by the bloom of a toxic fern.

customize.text: Archons, whose power is linked to Visions, have no need for such artifacts, as they possess their own innate elemental power and often draw energy from their Gnosis. However, some Archons use counterfeit Visions, which are just glass keychains, so as not to stand out among people. Adepti of Liyue also don't need a Vision because of their "illumination" and the light of a third "eye." They were born amongst the elemental energy that courses between heaven and earth. When Adepti, the pure elemental beings, take a human form, they use a Vision as a medium to harness elemental power to follow human rules. Certain astrologists are also capable of practicing hydromancy for the purpose of divination. Many other entities can likewise wield elemental power without the use of artifacts, including elemental lifeforms such as Slimes, Fungi, Oceanids, Hypostases, Eyes of the Storm, dragonkind, Phantasms, Cicins, and Fontemer aberrants. Beasts such as Regisvines and Whopperflowers absorb elemental energy through the Ley Lines, while some animals that have consumed the remains of powerful beings have evolved into sacred beasts capable of harnessing elemental forces. Samachurls can command elements and use ancient magic scrolls to cast spells, whereas Hilichurls, Hilichurl Rogues, and Mitachurls utilize items like Electro crystals, Slimes, flammable substances, or unmelting ice. Abyss Mages, Heralds, and Lectors are capable of utilizing elemental magic in battle.

Certain people employ specialized equipment that enables them to command the power of the elements. The Fatui, who serve the Tsaritsa of Snezhnaya, have long used Delusions, artifacts forged from the remains of deceased gods. The Delusions used by the Fatui have always been an unfinished product that drain the user's life force. Consequently, they could only be obtained upon request for a critical mission or in the event of an emergency. When the Fatui found it necessary to upgrade their combat strength for a confrontation with Ronova, the Ruler of Death, they developed an advanced type of Delusion by conducting experiments on Arlecchino, the heir to the Crimson Moon. Long ago, the authorities of Life, Death, Time, and Space all belonged to the moons. Of the three, the Iridescent Moon received the greatest share of the authority of Death. After the moons' demise, these highest authorities were reclaimed by the Heavenly Principles, who redistributed them among the Four Shades under a new system of rules. However, the broken Crimson Moon merged with the Abyss, which simulated its former authority, or, more precisely, the Abyss manifested the possibility that the authority had never been taken away in the first place. Thus, the authority of Death persisted in Teyvat in another form: within the Crimson Moon and its people's bloodline. Back in the days of Khaenri'ah, the Universitas Magistrorum never ceased its research into the Crimson Moon, and the Fatui later chose to continue these experiments, aiming to perfect their advanced Delusions and harness the latent potential concealed within the Crimson Moon. Drawing upon knowledge gained from the remnant of the past Sinner Hroptatyr, the Fatui completed the development of the Eye of the Fatui. This device harnesses the authority of the Crimson Moon as a conduit for the instantaneous release of power, capable of delivering a truly lethal blow. However, it makes no attempt to mitigate the side effects, such as the rapid depletion of one's life force. Consequently, only the people of Khaenri'ah, who are cursed with immortality, can wield the Eye of the Fatui, as ordinary humans would not survive the strain. It was for this reason that Pierro, a director of the Fatui, employed this artifact to strike down Ronova, the Ruler of Death.
Beyond their Delusions, the Fatui use specialized attire and weaponry that leverage technological advancements to manipulate elemental forces. The Eremites of Sumeru wield weapons that contain ominous, fragmented spirits, allowing them to use the power of the elements. In Inazuma, the Kairagi employ paper seals, created from a lost Kamuna art, to set their blades afire or infuse them with the power of lightning, while Treasure Hoarders and Nobushi often utilize elemental potions and powders in combat. Furthermore, certain automatons, such as the Maguu Kenki, landcruisers, or the Meks of Fontaine, are engineered specifically to harness elemental energy.

There are three realms in Teyvat: the Light Realm — the domain of the dragons, the Human Realm, and the
In ancient Khaenri'ah, where the inhabitants were unable to become allogenes, they studied the power of the Abyss and the "Seven-Shifting Serpent" technique, a minor spell developed by Khaenri'ah's Universitas Magistrorum. Through this technique, people can channel Abyssal energy to produce effects that mimic the natural elements. This is the method by which the Five Sinners and their disciples wield the power of the Abyss.

customize.desc: The great general of Watatsumi Island's forces. He is deeply trusted by his subordinates.

customize.name: Arataki Itto
customize.desc: The first and greatest head of the Arataki Gang, famed throughout Inazuma City's Hanamizaka... Wait, what? You've never heard of them? Are you trying to be funny here?

customize.name: Chiori
customize.desc: The owner of Chioriya Boutique. A tailor renowned throughout Fontaine.

customize.name: Kirara
customize.desc: A courier for Komaniya Express, a delivery company in Inazuma. A nekomata who loves her job and human society.

customize.name: Faruzan
customize.desc: A researcher from "one hundred years ago." She enjoys self-identifying as everyone's senior, and has significant knowledge of ancient scripts and machines of all kinds.

customize.name: Wanderer
customize.desc: A wayfaring figure whose identity is a mystery. He dresses like a mountain ascetic, but he certainly does not act the part.

customize.name: Dehya
customize.desc: A member of the Eremites, a mercenary organization that roams the sands of Sumeru. Valiant and powerful, she enjoys great fame amongst her fellow Eremites.

customize.name: Candace
customize.desc: A descendant of King Deshret with an amber left eye. The defender of Aaru Village.

customize.name: Nilou
customize.desc: The star of the Zubayr Theater. She is full of warmth and innocence, and her dances are lively and elegant.

customize.name: Layla
customize.desc: A Rtawahist student who specializes in Theoretical Astrology. Heavily prone to somnambulism and locked in a grinding war with sleep deprivation, the problem of restful slumber is a most troubling one to her.

customize.name: Cyno
customize.desc: The General Mahamatra in charge of supervising the researchers of the Akademiya. It is said that when he gets down to work, the General Mahamatra is even more efficient than the "Great Vayuvyastra" made by the Kshahrewar.

customize.name: Dori
customize.desc: An elusive merchant who has a fondness for glittering Mora.

customize.name: Sethos
customize.desc: The Temple of Silence's heir. Burdened with secrets, he comes from the sands.

customize.name: Tighnari
customize.desc: A young researcher well-versed in botany who currently serves as a Forest Watcher in Avidya Forest. He is a straight shooter with a warm heart - and a dab hand at guiding even the dullest of pupils.

customize.name: Collei
customize.desc: A trainee ranger active in Avidya Forest. Behind her enthusiastic words and actions hides a slightly introverted personality.

customize.name: Alhaitham
customize.desc: The current scribe of the Sumeru Akademiya, a man endowed with extraordinary intelligence and talent. He lives free — free from the searching eyes of ordinary people, anyway.

customize.name: Kaveh
customize.desc: A renowned architect from Sumeru who perhaps cares a bit too much about too many things. He is an aesthete troubled by reality.

customize.name: Lynette
customize.desc: A magic assistant of few words, her emotions are as inscrutable as any cat's.

customize.name: Chevreuse
customize.desc: The captain of the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol, who wears justice as an ever-present seal upon her heart. Her musket shall only ever point at the guilty.

customize.name: Furina
customize.desc: The absolute focus of the stage of judgment, until the final applause sounds.

customize.name: Sigewinne
customize.desc: A Melusine and the Fortress of Meropide's head nurse. She cares equally for every convict locked in the undersea prison.

customize.name: Wriothesley
customize.desc: Duke of the Fortress of Meropide, Lord Incognito of the murky depths.

customize.name: Escoffier
customize.desc: The ex-head chef of Hotel Debord, renowned throughout Fontaine as the Patissiere Supreme and vanguard of precision gastronomy. Has incomparably strict standards when it comes to cooking.

customize.name: Clorinde
customize.desc: An undefeated Champion Duelist. Sword in hand, she defends justice in the Court of Fontaine.

customize.name: Navia
customize.desc: The current President of Spina di Rosula, who is lovely, dutiful, and a great boss.

customize.name: Lyney
customize.desc: A famed Fontainian magician who possesses great stage presence as well as gift of the gab. Audiences are enthralled by his exquisite skills, and they hang on to his every clever word.

customize.name: Furina
customize.desc: The absolute focus of the stage of judgment, until the final applause sounds.

customize.name: Freminet
customize.desc: A reserved young man who is well-versed in diving. Beneath his distant, icy demeanor lies a pure heart bereft of all flaws.

customize.name: Charlotte
customize.desc: Reporter of The Steambird

customize.name: Emilie
customize.desc: A Fontainian perfumer, one who bottles secrets.

customize.name: Chasca
customize.desc: The Peacemaker of the Tlalocan, the ender of all disputes.

customize.name: Ifa
customize.desc: A vet from the Flower-Feather Clan who cherishes the life he leads alongside all manner of living things — people, animals, you name it.

customize.name: Mualani
customize.desc: A well-known guide in Natlan who owns a watersports shop, and expert in all forms of wave-chasing.

customize.name: Citlali
customize.desc: The great shaman from the Masters of the Night-Wind, the universally-revered Granny Itztli.

customize.name: Ororon
customize.desc: A young man from the Masters of the Night-Wind who instead lives in the wild alongside all manner of life.

customize.name: Varesa
customize.desc: A laid-back orchard manager and warrior of the Collective of Plenty. An aspiring hero who hungers for justice... and lots and lots of food!

customize.name: Iansan
customize.desc: Head coach of the fitness club at the Collective of Plenty, and a renowned Natlanese nutritionist.

customize.name: Kachina
customize.desc: A young warrior of the Nanatzcayan, given the Ancient Name of "Uthabiti." Kind-hearted and insatiably persistent, she grows stronger and more capable with each setback she faces.

customize.name: Xilonen
customize.desc: A Name Engraver of the Nanatzcayan, she is especially skilled at finding a good balance between the heavy responsibilities of her job and living well.

customize.name: Kinich
customize.desc: A Huitztlan Saurian Hunter skilled at counting costs.

customize.name: Mavuika
customize.desc: The leader of Natlan who inherited the Ancient Name of "Kiongozi." She made a vow to illuminate the future of the nation of war with the Sacred Flame.

customize.name: Jahoda
customize.desc: The Curatorium of Secrets' extremely reliable, do-it-all super employee (or so she claims).

customize.name: Aino
customize.desc: A genius mechanic and inventor from Nod-Krai who loves interesting machines and sweet treats.

customize.name: Illuga
customize.desc: Member of the investigation squad, the Nightmare Orioles. The youngest squad leader among the Lightkeepers.

customize.name: Arlecchino
customize.desc: "The Knave," Fourth of the Fatui Harbingers. A poised, ruthless diplomat. To the children in the House of the Hearth, she is their feared yet dependable "Father."

customize.name: Tartaglia
customize.desc: No. 11 of The Harbingers, also known as "Childe." His name is highly feared on the battlefield.

customize.name: Vodyanitsa
customize.desc: Prima Donna of the Korolevskiy Troupe and a Water Imp who has parted from her kin.

customize.name: Alyosha
customize.desc: A "professional hunter" and master of the Snezhnayan snowfields. A fierce, distinct "idealism" burns beneath his calm demeanor.

customize.name: Valeriy
customize.desc: Commander of the Special Assignments Battalion. A soldier skilled at protecting key personnel and keeping operations on track.

customize.name: Aloy
customize.desc: Formerly an outcast, now a hunter of unparalleled skill. Ready to do the right thing at any time.

customize.name: Ineffa
customize.desc: A multifunctional robot containing integrated mechanical components from various nations. The Source Core in her chest has endured the passage of countless years.

customize.name: Flins
customize.desc: A Lightkeeper of Nod-Krai, guardian of a lighthouse and graveyard on a northern isle. An enigmatic gentleman, cultured and courtly.

customize.name: Zibai
customize.desc: The White Horse Adeptus from Liyue's legends, known as Zibai. The most mysterious figure in Liyue's myths.

customize.name: Lauma
customize.desc: A Maiden blessed by moonlight and the grove alike, hope born to the Frostmoon Scions.

customize.name: Nefer
customize.desc: The remarkably resourceful owner of the Curatorium of Secrets.

customize.name: Vesna
customize.desc: Commander of the Druzhna and the Tsaritsa's keen blade.

customize.name: Sandrone
customize.desc: The Seventh of the Fatui Harbingers, "Marionette." Interprets all phenomena through the prism of mathematics, and is an elegant lady who is never absent from a tea party.

customize.name: Odette
customize.desc: A famed Snezhnayan ballerina who blossoms against the frozen landscape with a beauty as sharp as frost.

customize.name: Mitya
customize.desc: An exceptionally ingenious energy specialist and a master of the fine art of "schedule-dodging."
